To determine whether Ivan the Terrible used the Byzantine calendar, we can look at the historical calendar system in use in Russia during his reign (1533–1584).

1. During the medieval and early modern periods, the Russian Orthodox Church and the Tsardom of Russia used the Byzantine calendar (also known as the "Creation of the World" calendar or *Anno Mundi*).
2. In this calendar, the year numbering was counted from the creation of the world, which was placed at 5508 BC, and the new year started on September 1st.
3. Ivan the Terrible, as the Grand Prince of Moscow and the first Tsar of All Russia, dated his decrees, letters, and official documents using this Byzantine-derived calendar system (specifically, the Russian variant of it). 
4. Russia continued to use this calendar until Peter the Great reformed it to the Julian calendar and the Western European New Year (January 1st) in the year 1700.

Therefore, Ivan the Terrible did use the Byzantine calendar.

Final answer: Yes
